title: Vietnamese academic glossary and high-risk machine-translation audit

fallbackTranslationSpotCheck.method: Deterministic every-eighth-record sample of machine-translation-reviewed-fallback questions.

repeatedOptionReview.method: Most frequent repeated English option strings were grouped with all Vietnamese realizations to expose inconsistent or literal glossary choices.

limitations: This is a high-risk translation audit, not a claim that every naturalness issue in all 483 records has been copy-edited.

Several English source strings contain OCR corruption. Corrections marked source-en-ocr-corruption infer the intended reading from context and should be checked against the source slide before production replacement.
Suggested corrections preserve option order and do not change answer keys.

systemicFindings: Tuckman stage labels are translated literally and inconsistently; Performing as 'Biểu diễn' and Storming as 'Bão tố' can mislead learners.
Bloom Applying is repeatedly mistranslated as 'Đăng ký'; gerund labels also drift between progressive verbs and taxonomy-level names.
Power-with and Power-over are catastrophically mistranslated as electrical terms ('Cấp nguồn', 'Nguồn điện', 'Mất điện').
Meeting minutes, Recorder, Paralanguage, active voice and Referent Power contain answer-distorting homonym errors.
OCR debris survives inside several Vietnamese questions/options, including slide 18-related Tuckman variants and fallback translations.

severityDefinition.critical: Can reverse or hide the intended academic concept or make an option nonsensical.
severityDefinition.high: Materially damages academic accuracy or cross-question consistency.
severityDefinition.medium: Understandable but unnatural, ambiguous, or below the expected academic register.
